slot.brief: Given limiting molar conductivities of a strong electrolyte pair, assemble the limiting molar conductivity of a weak acid (or base) by addition and subtraction of the values.

stem: At the same temperature, $\Lambda_m^\circ$ for $\text{HCl}$, $\text{CH}_3\text{COONa}$ and $\text{NaCl}$ are $426.0$, $91.0$ and $126.4\ \text{S cm}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}$, respectively. What is $\Lambda_m^\circ$ for $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$?

verdicts.working: By Kohlrausch’s law, Λ°(CH₃COOH) = Λ°(HCl) + Λ°(CH₃COONa) − Λ°(NaCl) = 426.0 + 91.0 − 126.4 = 390.6 S cm² mol⁻¹.

working:
By Kohlrausch's law, $\Lambda_m^\circ(\text{CH}_3\text{COOH})=\Lambda_m^\circ(\text{HCl})+\Lambda_m^\circ(\text{CH}_3\text{COONa})-\Lambda_m^\circ(\text{NaCl})$.\n$=426.0+91.0-126.4=390.6\ \text{S cm}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}$.

Independent check: By Kohlrausch’s law, Λ°(CH₃COOH) = Λ°(HCl) + Λ°(CH₃COONa) − Λ°(NaCl) = 426.0 + 91.0 − 126.4 = 390.6 S cm² mol⁻¹.
